findings.claim: For fiscal 2026, ended September 3, 2026, Micron reported revenue of $133.188 billion versus $37.378 billion in fiscal 2025, GAAP net income of $84.969 billion, or $74.33 per diluted share, and fourth-quarter revenue of $54.229 billion with a GAAP gross margin of 86.8% and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $33.42.
findings.source_title: Micron reports record fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 results

findings.claim: Micron guided fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue to $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion, non-GAAP gross margin to about 86.25%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $38.15 plus or minus $1.00.
findings.source_title: Micron reports record fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 results

findings.claim: Fiscal 2026 DRAM revenue was $100.68 billion and NAND revenue was $31.79 billion, compared with $28.58 billion and $8.50 billion in fiscal 2025.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: In fiscal 2026 HBM3E 12-high was the majority of HBM shipments, Micron began volume production of HBM4 36GB 12-high and sampled HBM4 48GB 16-high, and it expects HBM4E volume to ramp in calendar 2027.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: In the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2026 Micron entered take-or-pay strategic customer agreements with multi-year volume commitments and price bands, and it said gross margins on those agreements should stay meaningfully above prior-cycle peak quarterly margins even at floor prices.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Micron received $12.75 billion of customer cash deposits in fiscal 2026 that are returned if purchase commitments are met and are mostly scheduled to be repaid between 2029 and 2031, and letters of credit of $7 billion at September 3, 2026 are not recognized as revenue unless a customer defaults.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: No single customer was 10% or more of fiscal 2026 revenue, but about half of revenue came from the top ten customers and about 60% came from the data center end market.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Cash and marketable investments were $73.45 billion at September 3, 2026, versus $11.94 billion a year earlier, while debt carrying value was $5.18 billion and $2.00 billion remained undrawn on the revolving credit facility; fiscal 2026 financing cash flows included $10.04 billion of debt repayments.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Micron estimates capital spending, net of government-incentive proceeds, at about $11.5 billion in fiscal first-quarter 2027 and about $25 billion in the first half of fiscal 2027, with spending higher in the second half, and it had $4.18 billion of property and equipment purchase obligations at September 3, 2026.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Revenue from customers headquartered in mainland China was $8.338 billion and from customers headquartered in Hong Kong was $6.289 billion in fiscal 2026, and the 10-K says the May 2023 Cyberspace Administration of China decision barring critical-information-infrastructure operators from buying Micron products continues to affect that revenue.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Micron names Samsung, SK hynix, Kioxia, Sandisk, CXMT, and YMTC as competitors and says Chinese state support for domestic memory makers, plus industry capacity adds, could produce DRAM and NAND oversupply and lower average selling prices.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Long-lived assets in Taiwan were $27.613 billion at September 3, 2026, the largest geographic balance, ahead of $14.463 billion in the United States and $12.345 billion in Singapore.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Receivables rose to $36.197 billion at September 3, 2026 from $9.265 billion at August 28, 2025, while inventories were $10.372 billion versus $8.355 billion.
findings.source_title: Micron reports record fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 results

findings.claim: Micron's CHIPS Act direct-funding agreements provide for up to $6.1 billion for planned fabs in Boise, Idaho and Clay, New York, plus up to $275 million to expand the Manassas, Virginia fab, for total grants of up to $6.4 billion, and the company also receives a 35% investment tax credit on qualified U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investment.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

findings.claim: Fourth-quarter GAAP results included a $500 million patent-license charge, and fiscal 2026 also included $511 million of losses on debt prepayments in the non-GAAP reconciliation.
findings.source_title: Micron reports record fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 results

findings.claim: The 10-K says memory average selling prices could fall materially if industry demand does not keep up with new fab capacity, and that China has restricted exports of certain rare-earth materials that Micron's suppliers need.
findings.source_title: Micron Technology Form 10-K for the year ended September 3, 2026

upcoming_catalysts.event: Fiscal first-quarter 2027 results against company guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion of revenue and non-GAAP EPS of $38.15 plus or minus $1.00. The September 30, 2026 release does not give the report date.
First DRAM wafer output at the Boise fab, projected for mid-calendar 2027, and initial product shipments from the acquired Tongluo, Taiwan fab beginning mid-calendar 2027.
HBM advanced-packaging capacity in Singapore expected to begin expanding in early calendar 2027.

policy_links.policy: CHIPS and Science Act direct funding and the 35% advanced-manufacturing investment tax credit
policy_links.bottleneck: U.S. leading-edge memory wafer and packaging capacity
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The agreements reimburse or credit qualified U.S. fab investment, up to $6.4 billion of grants plus a 35% tax credit. They are not disclosed as product purchase orders. Micron also signed a non-binding New York term sheet for up to $5.5 billion of credits and job incentives over 20-plus years.

policy_links.policy: May 2023 Cyberspace Administration of China decision that critical information infrastructure operators may not purchase Micron products
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The 10-K says the decision reduced Micron's ability to sell to customers headquartered in mainland China and Hong Kong, including direct and distributor sales. Fiscal 2026 still reports $8.338 billion of revenue from mainland-China-headquartered customers and $6.289 billion from Hong Kong-headquartered customers.

key_risks.risk: Gross margin reached 86.8% in fiscal Q4 2026. The 10-K warns that new industry capacity, including state-supported Chinese supply, can push DRAM and NAND into oversupply and cut average selling prices materially.
About 60% of fiscal 2026 revenue was data-center demand and about half came from ten customers, so a pause in AI data-center buildout would hit the business that produced the year's results.
The largest block of long-lived assets, $27.613 billion, is in Taiwan, so a disruption there would hit manufacturing that the company does not duplicate one-for-one elsewhere.

The CAC purchasing ban and possible further China action, plus China's restrictions on certain rare-earth exports, can reduce sales or constrain materials even though fiscal 2026 China-headquartered revenue was still material.

Customer deposits of $12.75 billion are liabilities Micron expects to repay from 2029 to 2031 if customers meet commitments, and fiscal 2027 capex steps up to about $11.5 billion in the first quarter and about $25 billion in the first half.

notes: No public equity offering, ATM, or convertible issuance was identified in the fiscal 2026 financing section. That section shows $10.04 billion of debt repayment, $1.13 billion of shares withheld for employee taxes, a $650 million repurchase of 2.5 million shares, and $610 million of dividends. Basic weighted-average shares were 1,127 million in fiscal 2026 versus 1,116 million in fiscal 2025. PricewaterhouseCoopers' report in the 10-K says internal control over financial reporting was effective at September 3, 2026. The September 30, 2026 release does not set the fiscal Q1 2027 earnings date; third-party calendars disagreed and were not used. CHIPS funding is disclosed as grants and a tax credit, not as product revenue, so evidence_of_company_revenue is false for that policy. Government-incentive cash proceeds of $3.316 billion appear in the fiscal 2026 cash-flow statement in the earnings release and are not all identified there as CHIPS grant revenue.
